sentences.text: Chaohusaurus is a basal ichthyopterygian that displays characteristics typical of the earliest ancestors of ichthyosaurs.
Unlike the dolphin-like shape of later relatives, this creature possessed a lizard-like appearance with an elongated body.
Its skeleton included roughly forty vertebrae located before the sacrum.
Adults featured a short head measuring about one-third the length of the trunk, equipped with a narrow, pointed beak and large eye sockets.
The mouth contained heterodont teeth, where blunt, pointed upper teeth sat opposite bulbous lower rear teeth.
It moved using flippers instead of webbed limbs, possessed an unusually long neck, and lacked a dorsal fin.
The tail fin had a wide base but remained low in profile.
This animal was among the smallest known ichthyosaurs, reaching lengths between 70 and 180 centimeters.
One reported specimen preserves the remains of three embryos.
Scientists suggest that the head-first birth method observed in Chaohusaurus indicates that viviparity first evolved in the land-dwelling ancestors of ichthyosaurs.
The genus was first described by Young and Dong in 1972.
The type species, Chaohusaurus geishanensis, was named that same year based on a fossil uncovered during railway construction.
The name Chaohusaurus honors Lake Chao Hu.
Fossils have been recovered from Chaohu and Yuan'an in China.
The holotype specimen was found within the Majianshan Limestone Formation, which dates to the Anisian stage.
Chen Lizhu named two additional species in 1985 using fossils from the same geological formation.
In 1998, researchers concluded that fossils previously identified as Chensaurus were actually juvenile Chaohusaurus forming a growth series.
Three further specimens were reported in 2014.
A Chinese-Italian paleontological project has since discovered eighty Chaohusaurus fossils.
The bulbous rear teeth in the lower jaw suggest a durophagous diet involving the crushing of shellfish.
Chaohusaurus is classified as a basal ichthyosauriform.
It belongs to the family Grippiidae.
The genus Chaohusaurus was established by Young and Dong in 1972.
The genus includes the type species C. geishanensis and the species C. zhangjiawanensis, which was described in 2013.
There is an ongoing debate regarding whether Chaohusaurus is a basal ichthyosaur or a non-ichthyosaurian ichthyopterygian, depending on the definition used.
A 2015 analysis by Motani and colleagues placed Chaohusaurus as basal to all other ichthyopterygians.
Some researchers note that Chaohusaurus technically falls outside the group Ichthyopterygia because the group definition has not been updated to reflect newer phylogenetic topologies.
Chaohusaurus lived during the Early Triassic period.
It inhabited the Early Triassic environment of what is now China.
It is debated whether C. chaoxianensis is a distinct species or a juvenile of C. geishanensis, with some researchers arguing it is a valid species.
